Where a roof lets water in.

Six places roofs fail. Most leaks start at one of them.

1 2 3 4 5 6 Ridge
  1. 1Ridge. Cracked mortar or loose ridge tiles let wind-driven rain in at the top.
  2. 2Chimney stack. Crumbling pointing and a cracked top let rain soak down through the brickwork.
  3. 3Lead flashing. Lifted or split flashing where the roof meets a chimney or wall lets water run straight in.
  4. 4Valley. Where two slopes meet, a worn lining or a blocked channel spills water into the timbers.
  5. 5Eaves. Slipped tiles or slates and worn underlay at the bottom edge soak the fascia and the top of the wall.
  6. 6Gutter. A blocked or sagging gutter overflows and sends water down the wall.

  1. A few slipped slates or a split flashing on an otherwise sound roof. Fix the fault and leave the rest alone.

    Ask about a repair

  2. Moss in the valleys, blocked gutters, tired pointing. Clear and re-point before they turn into leaks.

    Ask about maintenance

  3. Stains with no clear source, or a roof you cannot see. Survey the loft and the roof before anyone quotes.

    Ask us to take a look

  4. Battens rotting, slates delaminating, nails sliding. Past that point patching costs more than a new roof.

    Ask about a new roof

Under the part you can see

A roof works as a whole.

Tiles or slates, or whichever covering your roof has, are only the top layer. Underneath, each layer has its own job in keeping water out, so a good repair looks after all of them.

A recent project in Fairford

Roof
Cotswold stone-slate cottage, three gables
Problem
A failed lead valley by the chimney and slipped stone slates let water into the first-floor bedroom.
Work
Stripped the affected slope, relaid the valley in new lead and re-hung the slates, adding matching stone where needed.
Materials
Reclaimed stone slates, code 5 lead, treated battens, breathable underlay
Duration
Six working days

From first look to handover.

Four steps, always in this order, so you know what happens next.

  1. 01

    Inspect

    A look at the roof from a ladder or scaffold, then into the loft. Slates, ridge, valleys, flashings and gutters are checked and photographed.

  2. 02

    Quote

    A written quote that names the fault, the fix and the materials, and lists what is left out so nothing arrives as a surprise.

  3. 03

    Work

    Old tiles come off, new battens, underlay and tiles go on. The roof is planned so it is not left open overnight.

    If something new is uncovered, it is explained before any extra work is added.

  4. 04

    Handover

    Gutters and drive are cleared and you walk round the roof from the ground. Photos of the finished work follow.

Tell us about your roof

Three things you can check from the ground.

Stand in the garden or the street. Please do not climb up.

Tick each one off as you look.

  1. Slates and tiles

    Look along the roof for gaps, slipped or cracked pieces and green patches of moss.

    Slates and tiles looked at

  2. Chimney and lead

    Check the pointing, the pots and the grey lead strip where the stack meets the roof.

    Chimney and lead looked at

  3. Gutters and walls

    Look for stains below the gutter and plants growing from the joints.

    Gutters and walls looked at

Questions we get asked.

Anything else? Call 01632 960 482

Roofs sometimes hide rotten battens or a failed valley once the tiles are off. The usual approach is to stop, show you photos, explain the options and agree the cost in writing before any extra work starts.

A few slates or a section of ridge is usually a few hours to a day. A full re-roof on an average house is more often one to two weeks, depending on size and weather.

Beyond a small repair at low level, scaffolding is normally needed for safe access. It is often the largest single line on a roofing quote, so check whether it is listed separately.

Roofing stops in heavy rain, high wind and frost, because wet slates are unsafe underfoot and some materials will not bond. Expect dates to move with the forecast.

Ask for any guarantee in writing, with what it covers and for how long. New tiles and slates usually carry a manufacturer's guarantee. Cover for the workmanship varies from firm to firm.

Send photos and a few details through the form, or call. Most roofs need a visit before a firm price, because a photo cannot show the loft or the battens.
